cards.title: Your phone, three patients, zero confusion
cards.body: Many of us manage Mummy's thyroid, Papa's BP and Nani's sugar from one phone. Without a system, things blur fast.

cards.title: One folder or profile per person
cards.body: Never mix medicines across people. Separate photo folders, notes or profiles keep Papa's strips out of Mummy's list.

cards.title: Label with names, not just 'Papa'
cards.body: Use full name and age on records. At a hospital desk, 'Papa' means nothing, and two Sharma uncles can share a ward.

cards.title: Know each person's basics
cards.body: Allergies, major conditions, current medicines and the doctor's number. Keep a one-screen summary for each person.

cards.title: Ask first, keep it respectful
cards.body: Parents are adults. Agree together on what you manage and who sees what, especially with a crowded family group.

cards.title: Have a backup carer
cards.body: Share copies with one sibling or relative. If your phone dies or you're travelling, care shouldn't stop.

cards.title: One phone can hold a whole family
cards.body: Separate, labelled, agreed and backed up. AICA's family profiles are built to manage parents from one phone just like this.

takeaway: Keep one labelled profile per family member, know their basics, agree on access and always have a backup carer.
share: Managing Mummy, Papa and Nani's medicines from one phone? Keep a separate profile for each.
